correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs exact adjacency predicates, complete face enumeration as subsets of sixteen nine-point facets, explicit mod-two augmented boundaries, exhaustive Gaussian elimination of all matrices, and rank-nullity in every degree. Independent transpose implementation uses a determinantal-one coordinate transform for Shrikhande and a different enumeration; both compute identical f-vectors and ranks. Entire domain is finite, so enumeration is exhaustive, not merely experimental extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The theorem determines exact homology of complementary *open-neighborhood* complexes of a canonical cospectral strongly regular pair. Primary sources treating the same graphs investigate their clique complexes, not these homology matrices; dominance duality provides an equivalence of constructions but not this computation. Searches under equivalent non-dominating/Alexander-dual formulations and prior indexed results located no stronger implication. Priority remains subject to unindexed literature.
residual_risks: The 1959 graph-classification article could not be inspected in full; an equivalent unindexed numerical homology computation could exist.
The exact day of the earliest public release of the older 1959 graph paper was not verified; 2002-08-09 is the verified arXiv first-public date for the methodological primary source.
The earlier clique-complex, independence-complex, and domination-polynomial invariants already distinguish the pair by other methods; no first-distinguishing claim is made.

value.rationale: The two sixteen-vertex SRGs are precisely the natural exceptional pair sharing all strongly regular parameters and spectra. A complete degreewise homology classification of the same canonical complementary-neighborhood functor is structurally motivated and shows a new type of spectral insufficiency, with the specific nonzero degree-two rook class. It does not merely rename or recalculate existing clique/independence complexes or face-count polynomials; neither a broad theorem nor an unknown integral claim is needed.
